review.title: No delegation of local powers to private bodies
review.plain: The Legislature may not delegate to a private person or body power over county or municipal improvements, money, or property, to levy taxes or assessments, or to perform municipal functions. It may provide for deposit and investment of public moneys and for bond payment and registration.
powers: may, however, provide for the deposit of public moneys
may also provide for investment of public moneys in securities
limits: may not delegate to a private person or body power

provisions.what: The Legislature may not delegate to a private person or body power to make, control, appropriate, supervise, or interfere with county or municipal corporation improvements, money, or property, or to levy taxes or assessments, or perform municipal functions
forbids: Delegating to a private person or body power to make, control, appropriate, supervise, or interfere with county or municipal corporation improvements, money, or property
Delegating to a private person or body power to levy taxes or assessments, or perform municipal functions

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide for the deposit of public moneys in any bank, savings and loan association, credit union, or federally insured industrial loan company in this State and for payment of interest, principal, and redemption premiums of public bonds and other evidence of public indebtedness by banks within or without this State

It may also provide for investment of public moneys in securities and the registration of bonds and other evidences of indebtedness by private persons or bodies, within or without this State, acting as trustees or fiscal agents

review.title: Claims against counties and cities
review.plain: The Legislature may prescribe procedure for presenting, considering, and enforcing claims against counties, cities, and their officers, agents, or employees.
powers: may prescribe procedure for presentation, consideration, and enforcement of claims

provisions.what: The Legislature may prescribe procedure for presentation, consideration, and enforcement of claims against counties, cities, their officers, agents, or employees

review.title: Article XI restates earlier provisions
review.plain: Sections 1(b) (except its second sentence), 3(a), 4, and 5 of Article XI, on powers between the Legislature and cities and counties, restate the earlier Constitution with no substantive change. "General law," "general laws," and "laws" continue their earlier meaning.

provisions.what: The provisions of Sections 1(b) (except for the second sentence), 3(a), 4, and 5 of this Article relating to matters affecting the distribution of powers between the Legislature and cities and counties, including matters affecting supersession, shall be construed as a restatement of all related provisions of the Constitution in effect immediately prior to the effective date of this amendment, and as making no substantive change

The terms general law, general laws, and laws, as used in this Article, shall be construed as a continuation and restatement of those terms as used in the Constitution in effect immediately prior to the effective date of this amendment, and not as effecting a change in meaning

review.title: Voter approval for multi-county property taxes
review.plain: A local government formed after this section took effect, whose boundaries include all or part of two or more counties, may not levy a property tax unless a majority of its qualified voters voting on the tax approve it.
limits: shall not levy a property tax

provisions.what: A local government formed after the effective date of this section, the boundaries of which include all or part of two or more counties, shall not levy a property tax unless such tax has been approved by a majority vote of the qualified voters of that local government voting on the issue of the tax
provisions.binds: A local government formed after the effective date of this section, the boundaries of which include all or part of two or more counties
forbids: Levying a property tax without approval by a majority vote of the qualified voters
conditions: formed after the effective date of this section
the boundaries of which include all or part of two or more counties
exceptions: unless such tax has been approved by a majority vote of the qualified voters of that local government voting on the issue of the tax

review.title: Vehicle license fee revenues for local governments
review.plain: Vehicle license fee revenues from the rate up to 0.65 percent of a vehicle's market value go to the Local Revenue Fund and to cities and counties. If the Legislature lowers the fee below that, it must provide an equal replacement amount for them.

provisions.what: From the revenues derived from taxes imposed pursuant to the Vehicle License Fee Law, from that portion of the vehicle license fee rate that does not exceed 0.65 percent of the market value of the vehicle, an amount shall be specified in the Vehicle License Fee Law for deposit in the State Treasury to the credit of the Local Revenue Fund, for allocation to cities, counties, and cities and counties as otherwise provided by law
requires: An amount shall be specified in the Vehicle License Fee Law, or the successor to that law, for deposit in the State Treasury to the credit of the Local Revenue Fund
conditions: over and above the costs of collection and any refunds authorized by law
exceptions: other than fees on trailer coaches and mobilehomes

provisions.what: The balance shall be allocated to cities, counties, and cities and counties as otherwise provided by law
requires: The balance shall be allocated to cities, counties, and cities and counties

provisions.what: If a statute enacted by the Legislature reduces the annual vehicle license fee below 0.65 percent of the market value of a vehicle, the Legislature shall, for each fiscal year for which that reduced fee applies, provide by statute for the allocation of an additional amount of money that is equal to the decrease in the total amount of revenues otherwise required to be deposited and allocated under subdivision (a)
requires: provide by statute for the allocation of an additional amount of money that is equal to the decrease
That amount shall be allocated to cities, counties, and cities and counties in the same pro rata amounts and for the same purposes as are revenues subject to subdivision (a)
conditions: If a statute enacted by the Legislature reduces the annual vehicle license fee below 0.65 percent of the market value of a vehicle
for each fiscal year for which that reduced fee applies

review.title: Public Utilities Commission members
review.plain: The Public Utilities Commission has 5 members appointed by the Governor and approved by a Senate majority, for staggered 6-year terms. The Legislature may remove a member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption by a two-thirds vote of each house.
powers: The Legislature may remove a member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption

provisions.what: The Public Utilities Commission consists of 5 members appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate, a majority of the membership concurring, for staggered 6-year terms
conditions: a majority of the membership concurring

provisions.what: A vacancy is filled for the remainder of the term
The Legislature may remove a member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption, two thirds of the membership of each house concurring
conditions: two thirds of the membership of each house concurring

review.title: Commission procedures and hearings
review.plain: Subject to statute and due process, the commission may set its own procedures. A commissioner designated by the commission may hold a hearing or investigation or issue an order, subject to commission approval.
powers: the commission may establish its own procedures
may hold a hearing or investigation or issue an order

provisions.what: Subject to statute and due process, the commission may establish its own procedures
conditions: Subject to statute and due process

provisions.what: Any commissioner as designated by the commission may hold a hearing or investigation or issue an order subject to commission approval
provisions.holder: Any commissioner as designated by the commission
conditions: as designated by the commission
subject to commission approval

review.title: What are public utilities
review.plain: Private corporations and persons that run transportation, telephone and telegraph, or heat, light, water, power, storage, or wharfage systems for the public, and common carriers, are public utilities subject to control by the Legislature, which may add further classes.
powers: are public utilities subject to control by the Legislature
may prescribe that additional classes of private corporations or other persons are public utilities

provisions.what: Private corporations and persons that own, operate, control, or manage a line, plant, or system for the transportation of people or property, the transmission of telephone and telegraph messages, or the production, generation, transmission, or furnishing of heat, light, water, power, storage, or wharfage directly or indirectly to or for the public, and common carriers, are public utilities subject to control by the Legislature
terms: "public utilities": Private corporations and persons that own, operate, control, or manage a line, plant, or system for the transportation of people or property, the transmission of telephone and telegraph messages, or the production, generation, transmission, or furnishing of heat, light, water, power, storage, or wharfage directly or indirectly to or for the public, and common carriers

provisions.what: The Legislature may prescribe that additional classes of private corporations or other persons are public utilities

review.title: Transportation rates and charges
review.plain: The commission may fix rates and rules for transportation companies, prohibit discrimination, and award reparation for unreasonable charges. A transportation company may not raise a rate without a commission decision that it is justified, reviewable only as to confiscation.
powers: The commission may fix rates and establish rules for the transportation of passengers and property
prohibit discrimination
award reparation for the exaction of unreasonable, excessive, or discriminatory charges
limits: A transportation company may not raise a rate or incidental charge
shall not be subject to judicial review

provisions.what: The commission may fix rates and establish rules for the transportation of passengers and property by transportation companies, prohibit discrimination, and award reparation for the exaction of unreasonable, excessive, or discriminatory charges
A transportation company may not raise a rate or incidental charge except after a showing to and a decision by the commission that the increase is justified
forbids: Raising a rate or incidental charge
exceptions: except after a showing to and a decision by the commission that the increase is justified

provisions.what: This decision shall not be subject to judicial review except as to whether confiscation of property will result
exceptions: except as to whether confiscation of property will result

review.title: Legislature's plenary power over the commission
review.plain: The Legislature has plenary power, unlimited by the rest of the constitution but consistent with this article, to give the commission more authority and jurisdiction, set how courts review its actions, and enable it to fix just compensation for utility property taken by eminent domain.
powers: The Legislature has plenary power
to confer additional authority and jurisdiction upon the commission
to establish the manner and scope of review of commission action in a court of record
to enable it to fix just compensation for utility property taken by eminent domain

provisions.what: The Legislature has plenary power, unlimited by the other provisions of this constitution but consistent with this article, to confer additional authority and jurisdiction upon the commission
conditions: unlimited by the other provisions of this constitution but consistent with this article

provisions.what: The Legislature has plenary power to establish the manner and scope of review of commission action in a court of record
conditions: unlimited by the other provisions of this constitution but consistent with this article

provisions.what: The Legislature has plenary power to enable it to fix just compensation for utility property taken by eminent domain
conditions: unlimited by the other provisions of this constitution but consistent with this article

review.title: Commission powers over public utilities
review.plain: The commission may fix rates, establish rules, examine records, issue subpenas, administer oaths, take testimony, punish for contempt, and prescribe a uniform system of accounts for all public utilities subject to its jurisdiction.
powers: The commission may fix rates, establish rules, examine records, issue subpenas, administer oaths, take testimony, punish for contempt
prescribe a uniform system of accounts

provisions.what: The commission may fix rates, establish rules, examine records, issue subpenas, administer oaths, take testimony, punish for contempt, and prescribe a uniform system of accounts for all public utilities subject to its jurisdiction
conditions: for all public utilities subject to its jurisdiction

review.title: Free passes and commissioner conflicts
review.plain: A transportation company may not give free passes or discounts to state officeholders; a public officer, other than a Public Utilities Commissioner, who accepts one forfeits the office. A commissioner may not hold an official relation to or financial interest in anyone the commission regulates.
limits: A transportation company may not grant free passes or discounts to anyone holding an office in this State
shall work a forfeiture of that office
may not hold an official relation to nor have a financial interest in a person or corporation subject to regulation by the commission

provisions.what: A transportation company may not grant free passes or discounts to anyone holding an office in this State
forbids: Granting free passes or discounts to anyone holding an office in this State

provisions.what: The acceptance of a pass or discount by a public officer, other than a Public Utilities Commissioner, shall work a forfeiture of that office
exceptions: other than a Public Utilities Commissioner

provisions.what: A Public Utilities Commissioner may not hold an official relation to nor have a financial interest in a person or corporation subject to regulation by the commission
forbids: Holding an official relation to a person or corporation subject to regulation by the commission
Having a financial interest in a person or corporation subject to regulation by the commission

review.title: Local regulation of commission matters
review.plain: A city, county, or other public body may not regulate matters over which the Legislature gives the Commission regulatory power. This does not affect certain powers under city charters existing on October 10, 1911, or any city's right to grant franchises as prescribed by law.
limits: may not regulate matters over which the Legislature grants regulatory power to the Commission

provisions.what: A city, county, or other public body may not regulate matters over which the Legislature grants regulatory power to the Commission
provisions.binds: A city, county, or other public body
forbids: Regulating matters over which the Legislature grants regulatory power to the Commission
exceptions: This section does not affect power over public utilities relating to the making and enforcement of police, sanitary, and other regulations concerning municipal affairs pursuant to a city charter existing on October 10, 1911, unless that power has been revoked by the city’s electors
or the right of any city to grant franchises for public utilities or other businesses on terms, conditions, and in the manner prescribed by law

review.title: Article XII restates earlier provisions
review.plain: The provisions of this article restate all related provisions of the earlier Constitution and make no substantive change.

provisions.what: The provisions of this article restate all related provisions of the Constitution in effect immediately prior to the effective date of this amendment and make no substantive change

review.title: All property taxable at uniform value
review.plain: Unless this Constitution or federal law provides otherwise, all property is taxable, assessed at the same percentage of fair market value, and taxed in proportion to its full value.

provisions.what: All property is taxable and shall be assessed at the same percentage of fair market value
requires: shall be assessed at the same percentage of fair market value
exceptions: Unless otherwise provided by this Constitution or the laws of the United States

provisions.what: When a value standard other than fair market value is prescribed by this Constitution or by statute authorized by this Constitution, the same percentage shall be applied to determine the assessed value. The value to which the percentage is applied shall be known for property tax purposes as the full value
conditions: When a value standard other than fair market value is prescribed by this Constitution or by statute authorized by this Constitution
terms: "full value": The value to which the percentage is applied, whether it be the fair market value or not

provisions.what: All property so assessed shall be taxed in proportion to its full value
requires: taxed in proportion to its full value
exceptions: Unless otherwise provided by this Constitution or the laws of the United States

review.title: Taxation of personal property
review.plain: The Legislature may provide for property taxation of tangible personal property, stock, evidences of indebtedness, and interests in them, and by two-thirds vote may classify such property for differential taxation or exemption. Taxes on notes, stock, bonds, and similar interests may not exceed 0.4 percent of full value.
powers: may provide for property taxation of all forms of tangible personal property
may classify such personal property for differential taxation or for exemption
limits: shall not exceed four-tenths of one percent of full value
shall not be higher on personal property than on real property in the same taxing jurisdiction

provisions.what: The Legislature may provide for property taxation of all forms of tangible personal property, shares of capital stock, evidences of indebtedness, and any legal or equitable interest therein not exempt under any other provision of this article
exceptions: not exempt under any other provision of this article

provisions.what: The Legislature, two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring, may classify such personal property for differential taxation or for exemption
conditions: two-thirds of the membership of each house concurring

provisions.what: The tax on any interest in notes, debentures, shares of capital stock, bonds, solvent credits, deeds of trust, or mortgages shall not exceed four-tenths of one percent of full value
forbids: A tax on any interest in notes, debentures, shares of capital stock, bonds, solvent credits, deeds of trust, or mortgages exceeding four-tenths of one percent of full value

provisions.what: The tax per dollar of full value shall not be higher on personal property than on real property in the same taxing jurisdiction
forbids: A higher tax per dollar of full value on personal property than on real property in the same taxing jurisdiction

review.title: Property exempt from taxation
review.plain: Lists property exempt from property taxation, including state and local government property, public bonds, schools, libraries, religious worship, cemeteries, growing crops, young trees, a $7,000 homeowners' exemption, ships, household goods, debts secured by land, and $1,000 for certain veterans and their families.
powers: The Legislature may supersede the foregoing provisions with an alternative system or systems of taxing or exempting forest trees or timber
The Legislature may increase this exemption and may deny it
limits: This property is also exempt from special assessment
shall lose eligibility for the exemption

provisions.what: Property owned by the State is exempt from property taxation
Property owned by a local government is exempt from property taxation
exceptions: except as otherwise provided in Section 11(a)

provisions.what: Bonds issued by the State or a local government in the State are exempt from property taxation

Property used for libraries and museums that are free and open to the public and property used exclusively for public schools, community colleges, state colleges, and state universities are exempt from property taxation
conditions: free and open to the public
used exclusively for public schools, community colleges, state colleges, and state universities

provisions.what: Buildings, land, equipment, and securities used exclusively for educational purposes by a nonprofit institution of higher education are exempt from property taxation
conditions: used exclusively for educational purposes by a nonprofit institution of higher education

provisions.what: Buildings, land on which they are situated, and equipment used exclusively for religious worship are exempt from property taxation
conditions: used exclusively for religious worship

provisions.what: Property used or held exclusively for the permanent deposit of human dead or for the care and maintenance of the property or the dead is exempt from property taxation and also exempt from special assessment
exceptions: except when used or held for profit

provisions.what: Growing crops are exempt from property taxation

Fruit and nut trees until 4 years after the season in which they were planted in orchard form and grape vines until 3 years after the season in which they were planted in vineyard form are exempt from property taxation

Immature forest trees planted on lands not previously bearing merchantable timber or planted or of natural growth on lands from which the merchantable original growth timber stand to the extent of 70 percent of all trees over 16 inches in diameter has been removed are exempt from property taxation
terms: "mature" (forest trees or timber): at such time after 40 years from the time of planting or removal of the original timber when so declared by a majority vote of a board consisting of a representative from the State Board of Forestry, a representative from the State Board of Equalization, and the assessor of the county in which the trees are located

provisions.what: The Legislature may supersede the foregoing provisions with an alternative system or systems of taxing or exempting forest trees or timber, including a taxation system not based on property valuation

Any alternative system or systems shall provide for exemption of unharvested immature trees, shall encourage the continued use of timberlands for the production of trees for timber products, and shall provide for restricting the use of timberland to the production of timber products and compatible uses with provisions for taxation of timberland based on the restrictions
requires: provide for exemption of unharvested immature trees
encourage the continued use of timberlands for the production of trees for timber products
provide for restricting the use of timberland to the production of timber products and compatible uses with provisions for taxation of timberland based on the restrictions
exceptions: Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to exclude timberland from the provisions of Section 8 of this article

provisions.what: $7,000 of the full value of a dwelling, as defined by the Legislature, when occupied by an owner as his principal residence is exempt from property taxation
conditions: when occupied by an owner as his principal residence
exceptions: unless the dwelling is receiving another real property exemption

provisions.what: The Legislature may increase this exemption and may deny it if the owner received state or local aid to pay taxes either in whole or in part, and either directly or indirectly, on the dwelling
conditions: if the owner received state or local aid to pay taxes either in whole or in part, and either directly or indirectly, on the dwelling

provisions.what: No increase in this exemption above the amount of $7,000 shall be effective for any fiscal year unless the Legislature increases the rate of state taxes in an amount sufficient to provide the subventions required by Section 25
exceptions: unless the Legislature increases the rate of state taxes in an amount sufficient to provide the subventions required by Section 25

provisions.what: If the Legislature increases the homeowners’ property tax exemption, it shall provide increases in benefits to qualified renters, as defined by law, comparable to the average increase in benefits to homeowners, as calculated by the Legislature
requires: provide increases in benefits to qualified renters, as defined by law, comparable to the average increase in benefits to homeowners
conditions: If the Legislature increases the homeowners’ property tax exemption

provisions.what: Vessels of more than 50 tons burden in this State and engaged in the transportation of freight or passengers are exempt from property taxation
Household furnishings and personal effects not held or used in connection with a trade, profession, or business are exempt from property taxation
Any debt secured by land is exempt from property taxation

Property in the amount of $1,000 of a claimant who is serving in or has served in and has been discharged under honorable conditions from service in the United States Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, or Revenue Marine (Revenue Cutter) Service, served in time of war or in certain times of peace, and resides in the State on the current lien date is exempt from property taxation
conditions: is serving in or has served in and has been discharged under honorable conditions from service in the United States Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, or Revenue Marine (Revenue Cutter) Service

served either in time of war, or in time of peace in a campaign or expedition for which a medal has been issued by Congress, or in time of peace and because of a service-connected disability was released from active duty
resides in the State on the current lien date
exceptions: An unmarried person who owns property valued at $5,000 or more, or a married person, who, together with the spouse, owns property valued at $10,000 or more, is ineligible for this exemption

provisions.what: If the claimant is married and does not own property eligible for the full amount of the exemption, property of the spouse shall be eligible for the unused balance of the exemption
conditions: If the claimant is married and does not own property eligible for the full amount of the exemption

provisions.what: Property in the amount of $1,000 of a claimant who is the unmarried spouse of a deceased veteran who met the service requirement stated in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection 3(o), does not own property in excess of $10,000, and is a resident of the State on the current lien date is exempt from property taxation
conditions: is the unmarried spouse of a deceased veteran who met the service requirement stated in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection 3(o)
does not own property in excess of $10,000
is a resident of the State on the current lien date

provisions.what: Property in the amount of $1,000 of a claimant who is the parent of a deceased veteran who met the service requirement stated in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection 3(o), receives a pension because of the veteran’s service, and is a resident of the State on the current lien date is exempt from property taxation. Either parent of a deceased veteran may claim this exemption
provisions.holder: Either parent of a deceased veteran
conditions: is the parent of a deceased veteran who met the service requirement stated in paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection 3(o)
receives a pension because of the veteran’s service
is a resident of the State on the current lien date
exceptions: An unmarried person who owns property valued at $5,000 or more, or a married person, who, together with the spouse, owns property valued at $10,000 or more, is ineligible for this exemption

provisions.what: No individual residing in the State on the effective date of this amendment who would have been eligible for the exemption provided by the previous section 11/4 of this article had it not been repealed shall lose eligibility for the exemption as a result of this amendment
forbids: Loss of eligibility for the exemption as a result of this amendment
conditions: residing in the State on the effective date of this amendment
would have been eligible for the exemption provided by the previous section 11/4 of this article had it not been repealed

review.title: Adjusting veterans' exemption values
review.plain: In any year the assessment ratio changes, the Legislature must adjust the valuation of property described in subdivisions (o), (p) and (q) of Section 3 to keep the same proportionate values.

provisions.what: In any year in which the assessment ratio is changed, the Legislature shall adjust the valuation of assessable property described in subdivisions (o), (p) and (q) of Section 3 of this article to maintain the same proportionate values of such property
requires: adjust the valuation of assessable property described in subdivisions (o), (p) and (q) of Section 3 of this article to maintain the same proportionate values of such property
conditions: In any year in which the assessment ratio is changed

review.title: Exemptions the Legislature may grant
review.plain: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation, wholly or partly, the homes of certain disabled or deceased veterans and their spouses, nonprofit religious, hospital, or charitable property, property of certain named institutions, and parking for places of worship.
powers: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part

provisions.what: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part the home of a person or a person’s spouse, including an unmarried surviving spouse, if the person, because of injury incurred in military service, is blind in both eyes, has lost the use of 2 or more limbs, or is totally disabled, or if the person has, as a result of a service-connected injury or disease, died while on active duty in military service
conditions: if the person, because of injury incurred in military service, is blind in both eyes, has lost the use of 2 or more limbs, or is totally disabled
if the person has, as a result of a service-connected injury or disease, died while on active duty in military service
exceptions: unless the home is receiving another real property exemption

provisions.what: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part property used exclusively for religious, hospital, or charitable purposes and owned or held in trust by corporations or other entities that are organized and operating for those purposes, that are nonprofit, and no part of whose net earnings inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual
conditions: used exclusively for religious, hospital, or charitable purposes
that are organized and operating for those purposes
that are nonprofit
no part of whose net earnings inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual

provisions.what: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part property owned by the California School of Mechanical Arts, California Academy of Sciences, or Cogswell Polytechnical College, or held in trust for the Huntington Library and Art Gallery, or their successors

The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part real property not used for commercial purposes that is reasonably and necessarily required for parking vehicles of persons worshipping on land exempt by Section 3(f)
conditions: not used for commercial purposes
reasonably and necessarily required for parking vehicles of persons worshipping on land exempt by Section 3(f)

review.title: Exemptions cover property under construction
review.plain: Exemptions under Sections 3(e), 3(f), and 4(b) apply to buildings under construction, land required for their convenient use, and equipment in them, if the intended use would qualify the property for exemption.

provisions.what: Exemptions granted or authorized by Sections 3(e), 3(f), and 4(b) apply to buildings under construction, land required for their convenient use, and equipment in them
